hypotheses.description: Funding is not timing-neutral: holding a position through the once-per-epoch apply_funding debits collateral by the funding payment, while an intra-epoch straddler (no position at the scheduled funding event) is debited nothing. Scoped to the standard funding-scheduler assumption: funding is applied once per epoch at a single scheduled snapshot with no per-account retry after re-entry.
hypotheses.key_finding: Through the REAL reducer apply_funding (perp_v2/updates.py): a long base=100 at index $50k under a +cap (100 bps) rate has collateral_quote debited by funding_magnitude; a base=0 straddler is debited 0, so the intra-epoch round-trip strictly avoids a positive funding payment. The deviation is one-sided: the payer (long under +cap) loses and would straddle, the payee (short) receives a credit and would not. Confirmed through the real GUARDED engine.step: apply_funding is accepted and debits funding_magnitude for a position-holder reached via the guarded set_position action, but the guard REJECTS apply_funding on a flat account with the exact reason 'apply_funding requires non-zero position' (position_open_ok is the only failing gate condition) — so funding is conditioned on holding exposure at the funding moment, the precise timing lever. SCHEDULER SCOPE (model-honest): the escape is NOT unconditional. A rejected flat apply does not consume the epoch's funding slot (funding_last_applied_epoch advances only on a SUCCESSFUL apply), so the realizable guarded trace set_position(q) -> set_position(0) -> apply_funding(rejected) -> set_position(q) -> apply_funding(accepted, debits funding_magnitude) shows a re-entrant can still be charged later in the same epoch. The straddle escapes funding precisely when the trader is flat at the one scheduled snapshot; a retry-until-success keeper would re-expose a re-entrant. Model-scope characterization only; no keeper-policy remedy claimed.

hypotheses.description: The funding-straddle residual is bounded: the per-epoch avoided amount equals funding_magnitude and is at most floor(notional * cap / 10_000), tight when the funding rate sits at the cap.
hypotheses.key_finding: avoided = funding_magnitude(base, index, rate) <= floor(notional_quote(base, index) * funding_cap_bps / 10_000) over a witness family base in {1,7,100,9999} x cap in {1,25,100,500}, with equality exactly when the rate equals the cap. The bound follows from the real rate rule compute_funding_rate_bps saturating |rate| at funding_cap_bps and floor-division monotonicity.

hypotheses.description: Liquidation-size choice is not neutral: for an underwater position the partial-liquidation guard requires non-negative post-penalty collateral AND (when the residual is non-flat) that the residual restores maintenance margin, but it does NOT require the minimal sufficient fraction. The legal set is [f_min, BPS_SCALE]; a liquidator can full-close (max penalty) when a strictly smaller legal fraction already restores margin. The penalty scales with the closed notional and is transferred from the liquidatee into fee_pool/insurance.
hypotheses.key_finding: Witness through the REAL guard_partial_liquidate + apply_partial_liquidate: a long base=1e6 at index $1.00 with collateral 45_000 (< maint_req 50_000, > full penalty 20_000) is liquidatable. The auto-minimum fraction is 1667 bps (tight: 1666 bps leaves collateral non-negative at 41_668 but is GUARD-REJECTED because the residual fails maintenance margin, mreq 41_670 > 41_668 — so the guard enforces residual margin, lines 307-314), penalty 3_334, leaving a margin-compliant residual (coll 41_666 >= mreq 41_665). Full close (10_000 bps) is ALSO guard-legal, penalty 20_000. The liquidator's size choice extracts pen_full - pen_min = 16_666 extra, transferred from liquidatee collateral into fee_pool/fee_income (conservation: collateral loss == fee_pool gain). Exhaustive sweep over the whole legal range [1667, 10000] confirms every fraction is accepted and penalty is non-decreasing (strict between adjacent fractions). So the lever is 'oversize above the minimum sufficient fraction', not 'any fraction'. Research evidence only; the minimal-fraction enforcement remedy is an untested candidate, not claimed.

hypotheses.description: Settlement-boundary airtightness, VERIFIED not assumed (threat: free-look / settlement avoidance on the published clearing price). Split result. In-phase: no PRICE_PUBLISHED-phase-preserving action changes position_base (the only position-writing updates are set_position/partial_liquidate, both OPEN-gated, and settle_epoch, which exits to SETTLED). BUT the unconditional 'no reachable sequence' claim is FALSE: guard_advance_epoch checks only the epoch bound (no phase, no auth, no prior-settlement), so advance_epoch from PRICE_PUBLISHED skips settlement and reaches OPEN where set_position repositions — a reachable settlement bypass.
hypotheses.key_finding: Through the REAL engine.step + guards over a reachable PRICE_PUBLISHED state (reached via PUBLISH_CLEARING_PRICE). SUPPORTED in-phase part: set_position is guard-REJECTED for every target {0,500,999,1001,2000,-1000,-2000} in PRICE_PUBLISHED but ACCEPTED+effective in OPEN (guard_set_position requires OPEN, guards.py:150); over a broad action x param sweep from several reachable in-phase states, every phase-PRESERVING accepted transition leaves position_base unchanged (3-step trace confirms end-to-end); settle_epoch ignores any new_position_base (identical settled state for 7777 vs 0) and only deterministically zeroes a liquidatable position. FALSIFYING counterexample: guard_advance_epoch (guards.py:34) returns now_epoch+delta<=MAX_EPOCH only; apply_advance_epoch resets to OPEN WITHOUT settling, so a long at a 5% adverse clearing price who would lose 50_000 on settle_epoch instead ADVANCES (collateral 10_000_000 intact, epoch+1, OPEN) and closes via set_position(0) — avoiding exactly 50_000. So airtightness is CONDITIONAL on settle-before-advance lifecycle discipline that the pure-core guard does not enforce (cf. O-PT-01 scheduler scope). SEVERITY BOUND (verified, NOT live-exploitable): driven through the real shell entry apply_perp_ops, advance_epoch before settle is REJECTED with 'cannot advance epoch before settling current epoch' (src/core/perp_runtime_risk_gate.py:180) and allowed only after settle_epoch — so the invariant lives in the SHELL/runtime-risk-gate and the permissive guard_advance_epoch is a pure-core DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH gap only. Research evidence only; also gating advance on SETTLED in the pure core (defense in depth) is an untested candidate, not claimed.
